segments.text: A quiet Sunday morning in Hawaii.
At three forty-two, a minesweeper spots a periscope near the entrance to Pearl Harbor.
Far to the north, six Japanese carriers turn into the wind.
At six o'clock, the first wave takes off. One hundred eighty-three planes.
At six forty-five, the destroyer Ward fires on a small submarine. The first American shots of the war.
At seven oh two, a radar station on the north shore sees something huge.
More than fifty planes, a hundred and thirty miles out.
The officer on duty thinks they are American bombers, due from California.
Don't worry about it, he says.
At seven forty, the planes reach Oahu.
Below, eight battleships rest side by side. Sailors get ready for morning colors.
At seven forty-nine, the signal: attack.
At seven fifty-eight, a message goes out: Air raid, Pearl Harbor. This is not drill.
